cleanIntro:
This guide follows Kimber's bolt-action rifle manual, which does not name the Open Range Pro Carbon, so check your variant against it. Kimber prints one book for its bolt-action rifles; every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it.

The rifle strips to two pieces for cleaning: rifle and bolt. The bolt comes out past the bolt stop at the left rear of the receiver, and Kimber publishes one step past that — the cocking piece housing unscrews by hand so the inside of the bolt can be cleaned. Nothing else opens.

steps.title: Safety to position 2, finger outside the guard
steps.action: This guide follows Kimber's bolt-action rifle manual, which does not name the Open Range Pro Carbon, so check your variant against it. Point the muzzle somewhere safe and move the safety to position 2 — the middle position, where the safety is engaged and the bolt is still free to open. Keep your finger outside the trigger guard for everything that follows.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — OPERATION — Removal of the bolt, printed p.46

steps.title: Chamber and magazine proven empty
steps.action: Unload the rifle by the book's procedure for the magazine your rifle actually has — Kimber prints three, for a hinged floor plate, no floor plate, and a removable box magazine, and this guide does not choose one for you. Then open the bolt and look: chamber empty, magazine empty. If either holds a cartridge, stop here.
steps.aside: If the magazine is not removed (as applicable) and/or completely unloaded prior to cycling the bolt to clear the chamber, a cartridge in the magazine will be chambered when the bolt is closed.
steps.quote: Open the bolt and confirm the chamber and magazine are unloaded. Do not proceed unless unloaded.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — OPERATION — Removal of the bolt, printed p.46

steps.title: Bolt closed, then handle counter-clockwise and bolt to the rear
steps.action: With the rifle proven empty, close the bolt, then rotate the handle counter-clockwise to fully open and draw the bolt back. The close-then-open order is Kimber's own.
steps.quote: Rotate the bolt handle counter-clockwise to the fully open position and slide the bolt to the rear.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — OPERATION — Removal of the bolt, printed p.46

steps.title: Bolt stop pressed at the left rear — and mind the stock comb
steps.action: Find the bolt stop lever at the left rear of the receiver, push it in, and draw the bolt fully back and out. Guide it clear rather than levering it: the bolt passes close to the comb of the stock on the way out, and Kimber warns that catching it there marks the stock.
steps.aside: Special care should be taken to not contact the comb of the stock when removing the bolt as cosmetic damage could occur.
steps.quote: While pushing-in the bolt stop lever, pull the bolt fully to the rear and clear of the receiver.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — OPERATION — Removal of the bolt, printed p.46

steps.title: Field strip complete — and the bolt is stored separately
steps.action: Rifle and bolt is the whole field strip. Kimber asks that the bolt be kept apart from the rifle while it is being cleaned, serviced, transported or stored — a rifle with no bolt cannot chamber a round.
steps.quote: The bolt should be removed from the rifle and stored separately while cleaning, servicing, transporting or storing this rifle.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — OPERATION — Removal of the bolt, printed p.46

steps.title: Bore guide in, oiled patch from the chamber end
steps.action: Fit a bore guide and use a quality rod, and work from the chamber — the bolt is out, so there is no reason to enter at the muzzle and risk the crown. An oil-soaked patch goes through first to lift the loose fouling.
steps.quote: Using a suitable bore guide and quality cleaning rod, run an oil soaked patch through the barrel starting at the chamber.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CARE — Cleaning & Maintenance, printed p.50

steps.title: Solvent brush from the chamber end, out the muzzle
steps.action: After a solvent patch has soaked a few minutes and a dry patch has lifted the loose debris, run a solvent-wet bore brush from the chamber end out through the muzzle, several passes. Fit the brush after the rod is in the barrel and pull it out the muzzle — never drag a brush back through the bore. Patch until clean, then oil lightly, and run a dry patch before the next shot.
steps.quote: Run a bore brush wet with bore cleaning solvent through the chamber end of the barrel and out the muzzle, making several passes.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CARE — Cleaning & Maintenance, printed p.51

steps.title: Bolt, breech face and under the extractor
steps.action: Clean the bolt body and the breech face where the firing pin comes through, and get under the extractor — that is where carbon packs in and where extraction trouble starts. A toothbrush or similar nylon brush does the job.
steps.aside: Ultrasonic cleaning is not recommended. Damage to the finish or parts cleaned using an ultrasonic cleaner are not covered under warranty.
steps.quote: Clean the bolt and bolt breech face (where the firing pin exits), under the extractor, and anywhere else carbon and debris has built up (a toothbrush or similar nylon brush works well).
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CARE — Cleaning & Maintenance, printed p.51

steps.title: Bolt and receiver lightly oiled, bolt back in
steps.action: Lightly lubricate the bolt and the inside of the receiver, then reinstall the bolt the way Kimber describes. Lightly is the word — excess oil collects grit and reaches cartridges.
steps.quote: Lightly lubricate the bolt and the inside of the receiver.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CARE — Cleaning & Maintenance, printed p.51

steps.title: Chamber, breech face and ejection port wiped dry of solvent
steps.action: Wipe the excess cleaner and lubricant out of the chamber, off the breech face and out of the ejection port with a clean patch. Kimber's reason is the next cartridge: oil and solvent that reach a primer can cause a misfire.
steps.quote: To reduce oil and solvent contamination of cartridges, use a clean patch to remove excess cleaner and lubricant from the chamber, breech face and ejection port.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CARE — printed p.51

steps.title: Exterior wiped, lightly oiled, excess off
steps.action: Wipe the dirt off every exterior surface, give the metal a light coat of lubricant, then wipe the excess away. For damp, salty or long-term storage Kimber also recommends a rust preventative.
steps.quote: Wipe off all dirt on all exterior surfaces of the rifle.
steps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CARE — Cleaning & Maintenance, printed p.51

deepSteps.title: Partial bolt strip only — and it starts with the rifle proven empty
deepSteps.action: Kimber publishes exactly one step past the field strip: the bolt opens far enough to clean inside. Before it does, the same clearing sequence applies — safety at position 2, finger outside the guard, bolt open, chamber and magazine confirmed empty, and the bolt out of the rifle.
deepSteps.aside: If you believe that further disassembly is required, contact Kimber Customer Service or a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: The bolt should only be partially disassembled as outlined in this manual for routine cleaning.
deepSteps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — OPERATION — Disassembly of the bolt, printed p.37-38

deepSteps.title: Cocking piece housing unscrews counter-clockwise, by hand
deepSteps.action: With the bolt out, unscrew the cocking piece housing counter-clockwise out of the bolt body by hand — no tools, no vice. That opens the bolt enough to clean the inside of the body.
deepSteps.quote: Using your hand, unscrew the cocking piece housing counter-clockwise out of the bolt.
deepSteps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — OPERATION — Disassembly of the bolt, printed p.37-38

deepSteps.title: Housing back in clockwise, then the bolt back in the action
deepSteps.action: Screw the cocking piece housing clockwise back into the bolt until it is home, then reinstall the bolt in the action. That is the end of what Kimber publishes — anything further is Kimber Customer Service or a gunsmith.
deepSteps.aside: Insert the bolt back into the action, as described in “Installing the Bolt” section. (see page 45)
deepSteps.quote: Screw the cocking piece housing clock-wise into the bolt.
deepSteps.cite: Kimber Bolt Action Rifle Models Safety & Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — OPERATION — Disassembly of the bolt, printed p.37-38

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bore guide fitted; rod in at the chamber end
Oiled patch, then solvent patch to soak, then a dry patch
Solvent brush pulled out the muzzle, several passes; patch until clean
Light oil to finish; dry patch before firing

cleaning.name: BOLT
tasks: Bolt body and breech face cleaned
Do not use an ultrasonic cleaner — Kimber does not cover the damage

cleaning.name: CHAMBER & ACTION
tasks: Bolt and inside of the receiver lightly lubricated
Chamber, breech face and ejection port wiped free of solvent and oil

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STORAGE
tasks: Exterior wiped clean, lightly lubricated, excess wiped off
Rust preventative for damp, salty or long-term storage
Bolt stored separately from the rifle
Clean and lubricate every six months even if unused

reassembly: Cocking piece housing screwed clockwise back into the bolt body.
Bolt head slipped forward into the receiver, then pushed fully in.
Bolt handle rotated clockwise to the fully closed position; work it a few times to prove it runs.
Safety to position 2, then function check before any ammunition.
fncheck: Rifle empty, magazine empty, muzzle safe. Reinstall the bolt and work it several times — it should run and lock without drag, and the bolt stop should hold it in the receiver. Check the safety in each position: at position 2 the bolt opens and the trigger is blocked; fully rearward the bolt is locked. If the bolt binds or the safety behaves inconsistently, stop and contact Kimber rather than shooting it.
